facts.text: The SAT has Reading and Writing and Math sections, each scored 200–800. Total score: 400–1600.

Register through a College Board account and choose an available test center. Published weekend deadlines apply to U.S. and international students and expire at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. Device borrowing requires earlier registration/request, at least 30 days before test day.
Score Choice selects entire SAT test dates; some colleges require all scores. It is not available for the free score sends selected at registration or in-school testing.
Superscoring combines a student's best section scores across test dates when a college's policy allows it. It is a college policy, separate from Score Choice; verify each institution and program.

Take a timed Bluebook diagnostic now. Use Khan Academy and the official Student Question Bank for weaker skills. Consider March 6, 2027 for a first attempt, with May 1 or June 5 as an alternative. Avoid overloading the May AP period. Retakes depend on the diagnostic, chosen colleges and school workload.

Set strategic SAT targets from each shortlisted university’s published score distribution and policy. There is no verified universal Ontario-average-to-SAT target and no promised admission cutoff. A middle-50% range describes its specified cohort, not a requirement.

2027–28 SAT dates are officially labeled Anticipated. Registration deadlines and score-release dates for that cycle are not yet published on the reviewed schedule. Do not treat anticipated dates as confirmed.

For 2027 AP exams, the preferred school order date is October 2, 2026. Final orders for full-year, first-semester and exam-only sections are due November 13, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET. Spring course orders and fall order changes are due March 12, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Those dates are AP coordinator/school ordering deadlines, not a guaranteed student registration deadline. Schools set their own earlier deadlines, fees and outside-student policies. Contact a coordinator in October, join the correct section and confirm the actual exam order.

An AP course provides coursework; a standalone AP exam is a separate assessment. College Board allows most AP exams without taking the course, but recommends taking it. Arrange a test host; portfolio-based subjects have additional requirements. Exam-only preparation does not create an AP course on the school transcript.

AP scores range from 1 to 5. Many colleges award credit or placement for qualifying scores starting at 3, but the university sets the subject-specific rule. A 4 or 5 is a study goal only where supported by the chosen credit policy, never a universal admission requirement.
Regular 2027 AP exams run May 3–7 and May 10–14. Ask the coordinator for the reporting time and location; start-time rules changed in some locations for 2027.
The reviewed College Board exam schedule publishes 2027 dates, not 2028 dates. Mark 2028 subject dates as Not yet published; check again in Grade 12.

Use the four AP options below as a shortlist, not a requirement to take all four. Choose one or two aligned with strengths and available support before adding more. Protect Ontario course grades and prerequisite coverage.

If this Grade 11 student started Grade 9 in Fall 2024, the OSSD framework is 17 compulsory plus 13 optional credits, the literacy requirement, 40 community involvement hours, and two online credits unless the applicable opt-out/exemption is completed. Confirm the actual Grade 9 start year with guidance.

The financial literacy graduation requirement applies to students who began Grade 9 in 2025–26 or later, taking effect in Grade 10 Career Studies in 2026–27. Do not automatically apply it to the assumed Fall 2024 Grade 9 cohort.

U denotes University Preparation; M denotes University/College Preparation. Ontario offers destination-related Grade 11/12 courses. Meeting OSSD requirements is distinct from satisfying each U.S. university's subject and rigor expectations.

Keep Ontario marks in the school's original scale; do not invent a U.S. GPA conversion. Common App guidance says to leave cumulative GPA blank if the school does not calculate it or uses a scale unavailable in the form. Follow each university's specific transcript instructions.

You can prepare My Common Application answers, activities and the personal essay before the application year. College-specific questions and supplements should wait for the appropriate cycle and must be checked after rollover.

Early Decision is binding under the signed agreement; Early Action is nonbinding. Restrictive or Single-Choice Early Action limits other early applications according to the institution's rules. Read the actual agreement and financial-aid conditions before choosing ED.

Ontario residence or attendance does not establish citizenship. Application category, federal aid eligibility and entry documents depend on citizenship/immigration status and university rules. Display Citizenship-dependent until the student supplies status.

Canadian citizens generally do not need an F-1 visa stamp to enter as students, but must present a valid Form I-20 and be admitted in student status. The initial I-901 SEVIS fee still applies. Coordinate entry documents with the admitting school's international office; Canadian permanent residency alone is not Canadian citizenship.

Federal student aid generally requires U.S. citizenship or an eligible noncitizen category. Canadian citizenship alone does not make a student eligible; F-1 status is not an eligible category. Some exceptions exist, including certain Native American students born in Canada. Institutional aid is a separate school-specific question.

After admission and enrollment choice, request the I-20 through the school, confirm funding evidence, pay the required SEVIS fee, and follow citizenship-specific visa and entry instructions. Recheck government rules in 2028 before booking travel.

apPriorities.name: AP English Language and Composition
apPriorities.reason: Argument, source evaluation and revision align with humanities/social-science study and application writing.
apPriorities.difficulty: Writing-intensive; qualitative workload assessment, not an official difficulty rank.
apPriorities.timing: Grade 11 if writing is already strong and a host/course is available; otherwise Grade 12.
apPriorities.target: 4–5 for the current ASU example; not an admission requirement
apPriorities.credit: ASU currently gives 3 elective credits and placement into ENG 105 for 4 or 5; this is not automatic ENG 101 credit for a new first-year student.
apPriorities.status: Planning priority; verified content and credit example

apPriorities.name: AP Statistics
apPriorities.reason: Data analysis supports social sciences, psychology and business exploration.
apPriorities.difficulty: Quantitative reasoning and written explanations; first-year algebra is the current recommended prerequisite.
apPriorities.timing: Grade 11 or Grade 12 after appropriate algebra preparation; use the 2026–27 course framework.
apPriorities.target: 3+ for current ASU credit; 4–5 may preserve options elsewhere, subject to each university's table
apPriorities.credit: ASU currently awards 3 credits for STP 226 at scores 3, 4 or 5.
apPriorities.status: Planning priority; verified prerequisite and credit example

apPriorities.name: AP Psychology
apPriorities.reason: A coherent option for students exploring psychology, sociology or broader social sciences.
apPriorities.difficulty: Substantial concepts and research interpretation; no formal College Board prerequisite. This is not a promise that the course is easy.
apPriorities.timing: Grade 11 if supported and manageable; otherwise Grade 12.
apPriorities.target: 4–5 for the current ASU example; not an admission requirement
apPriorities.credit: ASU currently awards 3 credits for PSY 101 at scores 4 or 5.
apPriorities.status: Planning priority; verified content and credit example

apPriorities.name: AP Human Geography
apPriorities.reason: Population, migration, culture and cities connect directly with sociology and broader social-science interests; map and data interpretation complement Psychology and Statistics.
apPriorities.difficulty: Reading, geographic vocabulary, map/data analysis and written explanations require steady practice. This workload advice is editorial, not an official difficulty ranking.
apPriorities.timing: Consider Grade 11 or Grade 12 when social-science reading is comfortable and a course or exam host is available.
apPriorities.target: Consider 4–5 as a study goal; not an admission requirement or a universal credit threshold
apPriorities.credit: Check each university’s Human Geography credit and degree requirements before registering; no specific credit award is assumed here.
apPriorities.status: Optional planning priority; verified course content and exam date
